A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMSAE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original debiasing experiments on multilingual BiasBios, Twitter Hate Speech and MSEFair, including accuracy and fairness results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical results, including the extensive appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: The language-subset procedure, SVD erasure and projection updates in Figure 4 remain unchanged. The newly specified k=2 documents an implementation choice without establishing a change to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same multilingual profession-prediction, hate-speech-recognition and helpfulness-prediction tasks, with unchanged datasets, language coverage and protected attributes. Newly cited application domains are not evaluated.

E2.justification: SAL, INLP, SentenceDebias and FullyJoint retain their roles in the corresponding comparisons, including the appendices. Newly discussed activation-editing methods are cited but not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Data splits, model configurations, accuracy and TPR-Gap metrics, final-layer probing and projection ordering are retained. The k=2 and LogisticRegression max_iter=1000 statements are newly disclosed settings, not revisions to previously specified settings.

E4.justification: The projection-order discussion, embedding visualizations and comparisons between monolingual, FullyJoint and subset configurations are retained. Expanded captions and theoretical discussion introduce no new ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The table annotations remain changes relative to baseline scores, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Section 6.2.1 corrects the language associated with the 6.2-point IMSAE and 1.2-point monolingual race-bias reductions from Spanish to Polish. This matches the unchanged Table 4 Polish TPR-Gaps of 6.2, 0.0 and 5.0, respectively. Numerical table entries throughout both PDFs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a rank-2 cross-covariance assertion for binary protected attributes. Section 4 adds the mathematical qualification that sequential projections do not compute the intersection of their ranges. Assumption 1 and the existing covariance derivation remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: iterative multilingual attribute erasure, transfer without target-language data, the MSEFair dataset and improved debiasing while preserving utility. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies reliance on final-layer representations as a limitation and leaves layer-wise analysis to future work. The expanded Figure 3 caption also interprets increased mixing with residual separability as supporting the language-mixture assumption.

D1.justification: v2 specifies k=2 and common LogisticRegression settings with max_iter=1000. It also adds an explicit code URL in the abstract footnote; v1 only mentions a GitHub repository in Appendix B.3. These are documentation and access-information additions.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and brief positioning relative to SEA, Sparse Activation Editing and diffusion-model representation editing, alongside references concerning projection intersections, multilingual representations and layer-wise information. The central positioning as a structural extension of SAL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanatory additions, spelling and terminology corrections, an added author affiliation and revised acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 4 receive expanded captions, with associated text reflow and minor caption and typography adjustments elsewhere. The same four figures and nineteen tables remain, without redesigned plots or substantive table restructuring.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through the explicit code URL, classifier settings, corrected Polish result attribution and final-layer limitation. The experimental tables remain unchanged. The gains are qualified by an unresolved inconsistency between the new rank-2 rationale in Section 3 and the retained rank-1 discussion in Section 4.
